1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.c4 Nc6 4.d4 cxd4 5.Nxd4 Qc7 6.Nc3 a6 7.Be2 Nf6 8.O-O 
Bb4 9.Nxc6 bxc6 10.Qc2 Bc5 11.Kh1 Bd4 12.Bg5 h6 13.Bh4 g5 14.Bg3 e5 15.
Rad1 {The game has already begun rather idiosyncratically, with the White 
lead in development apparently offset by Black's control of the key 
central squares and the break f2-f4. However, Ganbold barely seems to 
notice the fact that in a few moves time he will be a rook down.} 15...d6 
16.Rxd4!? {A sacrifice so bold that it deserves to work, even if it 
shouldn't. Banikas must have felt quite confident once he had settled down
to life a rook up, only to be bowled over by a stunning piece of brute 
force tactics. Seriously considering such a brave course of action during 
a game deserves rewards in itself. Most players wouldn't consider a move 
like this even during analysis!} 16...exd4 17.c5 dxc3 18.Bxd6 Qd8 
    ( 18...Qa5 19.f4 {and the magnitude of the attack is debatable.} )
19.Qxc3 Rg8 {White has a mighty bishop on d6, untouchable for the moment 
at least, but it cannot give mate on its own. The black king is caught in 
the centre and White controls all the dark squares, but something must be 
done before these advantages wane.} 20.f4! {Opening lines.} 20...gxf4 21.
Rxf4 Rg6 
    ( {Given White's thunderous refutation of the move played} 21...Nh7 {
    is necessary.} )
22.Bh5!! Rg5 
    ( 22...Nxh5 23.Qh8+ Kd7 24.Rxf7+ Ke6 25.Qxd8 Kxf7 26.Qf8+ Ke6 27.Qe7# 
    )
23.Rxf6 Rxh5 24.Rg6!! Rg5 
    ( 24...fxg6 25.Qh8+ Kd7 
        ( 25...Kf7 26.Qxd8 {simply wins} )
    26.Qh7+ Ke6 27.Qxg6+ Qf6 
        ( 27...Kd7 28.Qf7+ Qe7 29.Qxe7# )
    28.Qe8+ Qe7 29.Qxe7# )
    ( 24...Kd7 25.Qg7 Qe8 26.Rf6 )
25.Qh8+ Kd7 26.Qh7 Qe8 27.Rf6 Kd8 28.Rxf7 {After a fantastic forcing 
sequence, the threats are unanswerable.} 28...Bd7 {To prevent Bc7 mate.} 
29.Re7 Re5 {Every little while somebody produces one of those sacrifices 
that knocks you off your chair, a sacrifice so bold that it deserves to 
work, even if objectively it probably shouldn't. Bankias must have felt 
quite confident once he had settled down to life a rook up, only to be 
bowled over by a stunning piece of brute force tactics.} 
    ( 29...Qf8 30.Rxd7+ )
1-0

against the bishop pair. Here both players appeared to agree that any such
exchange will greatly damage white's attacking prospects. However, the 
upshot of avoiding the exchange is that black obtains an excellent 
diagonal free of charge. My feeling is that white should react in a less 
commital manner, at which point alternatives to avoiding the exchange

mir aussichtsreicher.} 
    ( 5.e3 $142 !? Nc6 6.cxd5 
        ( 6.Be2?! d4 =+ )
    6...exd5 7.Bb5 
        ( 7.Be2 )
        ( 7.d4 )
    )
5...Nc6 6.Bg2 d4 {Schwarz hat spuerbar Raumvorteil im Zentrum. Der Bb2 
steht passiv.} 7.O-O

        ( 7...Bd6 8.Nbd2 h6 9.O-O O-O 10.Re1 e5 11.h3 Re8 12.Qc2 Nb4 13.
        Qb1 Bd7 14.a3 Nc6 15.Nh2 Qc8 16.g4 h5 {0-1

    15.Bc1 Nh5 16.g4 Nf4 {0-1 Bathie,N-Mikhalevski,V/Mamaia 1991/CBM 25 
    ext (54)} )
7...Bd6?! 
    ( 7...e5 =+ {Dieser Zug waere logisch, denn nach 8.e3 kann Schwarz 
    z.B. 8...Be7 ziehen.} )
8.e3 e5 9.exd4 cxd4 {Wir haben eine Stellung fuer die Benoni-Verteidigung 
typische Stellung vor uns. Schwarz verfuegt ueber ein starkes 
Bauernzentrum, aber in dieser asymmetrischen Stelluing bekommt Weiss seine
Gegenchancen am Damenfluegel.} 
    ( 9...exd4 10.Re1+ Be7 11.d3 = )
10.d3 O-O 11.Ba3 {Eine gute Idee - Weiss verliert zwar Zeit mit diesem 
Laeuferzug (erst Bb2 und dann Ba3), aber da der Bb2 passiv ist, moeche 
Weiss ihn abtauschen.} 
    ( 11.Na3 )
11...Re8 12.Re1 Bf5 
    ( 12...Bg4 = )
13.Nh4 Bg4 14.Qc1 Bxa3?! {Dieser Laeuf ertausch aus freien Stuecken 
gefaellt mir nicht. In der Folge hat Weiss keine Probleme, seine 
Entwicklung zu beenden.} 
    ( 14...Rc8!? )
15.Nxa3 = Qa5?! 
    ( 15...Rc8 )
16.h3 Bd7 17.Nb5 Nb4 {Dieser Zug scheint zunaechst sehr stark, in 
Wirklichkeit aber bekommt Weiss dadurch gute Gegenchancen.} 18.Qd2 Bxb5 
19.cxb5 Qxb5 20.Nf5 ~= {Weiss hat einen Bauern weniger, aber sein

unteliegen, dann haette der slowenische Grossmeister die Partie hier schon
aufgegeben.} 23.Nxb5

    ( 3...gxf6 4.e3 c6 
        ( 4...c5 5.dxc5 Nc6 6.Nc3 e6 7.Qh5 Bd7 8.O-O-O b6 9.cxb6 Qxb6 10.

        {1-0 Plaskett,J-Jonkman,H/Mondariz ESP 2000/The Week in Chess 306

    5.c4 e6 6.Nc3 Nd7 7.cxd5 cxd5 8.Nf3 a6 9.Bd3 f5 10.g3 Bd6 11.Qb3 Rb8 
    12.O-O O-O 13.Rfc1 Qe7 14.Ne2 b5 15.Nf4 Nb6 16.Qd1 ~ {0-1 
    Rogers,I-Ghaem Maghami,E/Istanbul TUR 2000/The Week in Chess 313 (50)}

4.e3 Bd6 {In exchange for the double pawns, Black has two bishops and a 
free game.} 5.c4 {Anoter plan here is by not playing c4, but preparing the
long castling by Bd3, Qf3, Nd2 etc.} 5...dxc4 
    ( 5...c6 6.cxd5 cxd5 7.Nc3 Be6 8.Qb3 Qd7 += {1-0 
    Palatnik,S-Mamalakis,G/Iraklion 1992/EXT 99 (37)} )
6.Bxc4 O-O 7.Nc3 f5 {With two ideas: to post the knight on f6 and e4 in 
the future or to play f5-f4 and get rid of the double pawn.} 8.Nge2 {
Preventing f5-f4.} 8...Nd7 9.Qc2 Nf6 10.O-O-O a6 {Black is preparing a 
counterplay on the queenside.} 11.h3 g6 12.Bb3 b5 13.g4 {Otherwise Black 
would achieve a good position with Bb7, Qe7 and c5.} 13...Bb7 
    ( 13...fxg4 14.hxg4 Bxg4 15.e4 ~= )
14.gxf5?! {It looks like White is overevaluating his sacrifice. He should 
have played:} 
    ( 14.Rhg1 {For example:} 14...fxg4 15.hxg4 b4 16.Na4 Qe7 17.Nc5 Bf3 {
    With a double-edged play.} )
14...b4 15.Na4 Be4 {To release the pressure on g6.} 16.Qc4 Bxh1 17.Rxh1 
Qe7 18.fxg6 hxg6 19.Bc2 Kg7 20.Rg1 
    ( 20.Nc5 Bxc5 21.dxc5 
        ( 21.Qxc5 Qxc5 22.dxc5 Rh8 23.Nf4 Rae8 -+ )
    21...a5 {With Rae8 and Ne4} )
20...Rh8 21.Qc6 
    ( 21.Ng3 Bxg3 22.Rxg3 Ne4 23.Bxe4 Qxe4 24.Qxb4 Qh1+ -/+ )
21...Rae8 22.Qf3 
    ( 22.Qxa6 Rxh3 {White has n o serious counter play against Reh8 and 
    Rh1. His knights cannot move.} )
22...Ne4 {With Na4 out of the game White is helpless.} 23.Rg4 
    ( 23.Bxe4 Qxe4 24.Qxe4 Rxe4 -+ {Wins easily for Black.} )
23...Rh4! {Exchanging pieces is the simplest way to implement the 
advantage.} 24.Qg2 
    ( 24.Bxe4 Rxg4 25.hxg4 Qxe4 -+ )
    ( 24.Rg1 Reh8 25.Bxe4 Rxe4 -+ )
24...Rxg4 25.hxg4 Ng5 26.Qd5 Ne4 27.Qxe4 
    ( 27.f3 Nf6 -+ )
27...Qxe4 28.Bxe4 Rxe4 29.g5 Be7 30.Kd2 Bxg5 31.Nc5 Re7 32.Nxa6 Bh4 33.
Nxb4?! {Makes it easier for black .} 
    ( 33.Ke1 Rxe3 34.Nxb4 Rf3 -+ )
    ( 33.f4 b3 34.axb3 Bf2 -+ )
    ( 33.Ng3!? b3 34.axb3 f5 {Black finally should win.} )
33...Bxf2 34.Nd5 Re8 35.Nxc7 Rxe3 {Once the position is open, The majority
of the bishop and rook over the knights is felt strongly.} 36.a4 Rb3 37.
Kc2 Rb7 38.Nb5 g5 39.Nd6 Rd7 40.Ne4 
    ( 40.Nf5+ Kf6 41.Nfg3 Bxg3 42.Nxg3 Rxd4 -+ )
40...Bxd4 41.Nxg5 Bxb2! 42.Nf3 
    ( 42.Kxb2 Rd2+ 43.Kc3 Rxe2 -+ )
42...Ba1 43.Nd2 Re7 44.Ng3 Rc7+ 45.Kb1 Be5 46.Nge4 Bf4 {Black will 
exchange his bishop for one of White's knights, and if White avoids that 
he will loose the a-pawn.} 0-1
